approach: Add an optional `mirrored_sources` section to the job plan. An entry has `content`, `source`, `places` (every place in the source the content depends on) and `comparison` (the number of the criterion whose demonstration compares the written content to every place, not only its structure). A new admission rule, `mirrored_sources_findings(mirrors, criteria)`, called from `plan_findings` after `dependents_findings`, raises one major finding per fault: blank `content` or `source`, no non-blank place, or `comparison` of 0 or above the criteria count. A major finding sends the plan back to the planner with no critic call, as `dependents` does. An empty or missing list means the plan mirrors nothing and gives no finding. The section is stored on `JobPlan` with `serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")` and shown by `plan_body` only when non-empty, so old records and plans serialise and render as before. The planner.md bullet itself states the whole rule: the source is named, every dependent place is listed (each term mention, each compiled-in cache-key file), and a demonstration compares the content to each place, not only its structure. To make room under the 700-token frame limit, the producer trims a few non-protected words in other planner.md lines. The critic.md bullet tells the critic to reject (major finding) a plan that mirrors content without the named source, the complete list or a comparing demonstration. Admission checks shape only. Completeness and structure-only comparisons are the critic's check and are marked prose-only in the prompts, the design doc and the CHANGELOG, so the shape rule is not read as closing class f62n.

decisions.choice: Structured plan section with an admission shape rule, plus a critic prompt rule for what a shape check cannot see.
decisions.reason: The critic is a model, so a rejection of a plan with no list is not deterministic; a tested admission finding is. The defaults say a rule that matters is enforced by mechanism or marked prose-only. `dependents` is the model: admission checks shape, the critic checks completeness against its own search.

rejected.why: A fixture cannot make a model critic reject, so the rejection could not be tested and the request asks for a rejected fixture.

rejected.option: Fold the list into `dependents` with a new DependentKind variant
rejected.why: One entry per place cannot show a source with no places, and an entry has no field for the comparing criterion, so the fixture would have nothing to reject.

rejected.option: Detect mirroring by keywords in the plan text or the reading (mirror, cache key, seed, definition)
rejected.why: The keywords hit unrelated plans, including this one, so refusals would rise on a guess. Whether a plan mirrors a source is the planner's declaration, backed by the critic.

decisions.choice: The section is `Vec<PlanMirror>`; an empty list or a missing key means the plan mirrors nothing and gets no finding.
decisions.reason: Most plans mirror nothing. The existing plan JSON fixtures (crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs:379, crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs:2669, introspection.rs:737, crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs:794, job_plan.rs:431) stay valid with no edits, and old records re-serialise byte for byte.

rejected.option: Require the section and refuse an empty list like `dependents`
rejected.why: Most plans would be refused or padded, and the JSON fixtures in non-deliverable crates would need edits.

rejected.option: `Option<Vec<_>>` so a missing key can be refused
rejected.why: It separates 'forgot' from '[]' but every JSON fixture would need the key. The critic prompt covers 'forgot'.

decisions.choice: The comparison is checked for shape only: the number is 1 to the criteria count. The no-demonstration case is not re-checked by the new rule.
decisions.reason: `plan_findings` already raises a major finding for any in-range criterion without exactly one demonstration (admission.rs:180-198); a second finding for the same fault would duplicate it. Whether the demonstration compares content to every place stays with the critic, since a keyword check of demonstration text would be a guess.

rejected.option: Keep the no-demonstration check in the new rule
rejected.why: It duplicates an existing finding on the same fault.

rejected.option: Require the demonstration's `observes` to contain every place string
rejected.why: A place is often a long description, so the check would refuse good plans and pass a stuffed one.

decisions.choice: Put the complete rule in the planner.md bullet (source named, every dependent place listed with the two examples, a comparing demonstration, 'not only its structure'), and in the `PlanMirrorOutput` field docs as well. Make room by trimming non-protected words in other planner.md lines, not by raising the 700-token frame limit. (Answers finding 9.)
decisions.reason: Criterion 1 is about planner.md, so the text must be there, not only in the schema docs. The frame test (crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:404) needs each frame under 700 tokens, which is at most 2097 bytes; planner.md is 1918, so 179 bytes remain and the full bullet is about 205 bytes. Line 6 ('Prefer the smallest design for the goal'), line 13 ('what fails without the behavior') and the 'Each entry has name, dependent, kind...' sentence in line 11 can lose about 40 bytes without dropping a rule. Wording kept verbatim because tests read it: lib.rs:466-468 ('calling an external service (GitHub API, CI run, deploy)', 'must name the state it needs', 'how the plan checks or waits for it'), briefs.rs:2398-2403 ('seam, fake or fixture', 'Never put the logic under test inside the double', 'refusal_corpus'). rejected.option: Keep the short bullet and leave the rule to the schema docs
rejected.why: It omits 'not only its structure' and the examples that criterion 1 requires planner.md to state.

rejected.option: Raise the 700-token frame limit in lib.rs
rejected.why: It is a guard on prompt size and out of scope; the rule fits once a few words are trimmed.

decisions.choice: No mechanical path check on `places`; completeness is prose-only.
decisions.reason: `plan_findings` has only an `is_directory` callback, not a file-exists callback (admission.rs:172-177). A place may live in a brief or a request, not a repository file, so a path rule would refuse good plans. The mechanism catches an empty list. The CHANGELOG, the design doc and the prompts say that admission checks shape and the critic's own search covers completeness (answers finding 13).

rejected.option: Require each place to start with a relative path and check it against the base
rejected.why: Needs a new existence callback, breaks for sources outside the repository, and cannot tell a complete list from a partial one.

rejected.option: Check that each place contains a path-like token
rejected.why: Refuses prose places such as 'the Definitions section of the brief' and passes a vague 'foo.rs'.

decisions.choice: Show the section in `plan_body` (briefs.rs) only when non-empty.
decisions.reason: The critic cannot judge a list it is not shown and the producer needs the places. When empty, the rendered bytes are unchanged, so producer-section hashes still match. `VerifierPlan::from_plan` (briefs.rs:1186) copies only demonstrations and files, so the verifier view is unaffected.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of planner.md. The producer's final wording must match the bullet checked here, which is: `- mirrored_sources: content mirroring a governing source: name it and list every place it depends on (each term mention, each compiled-in cache-key file); a demonstration compares content to each, not only structure.` (final wording may differ slightly but must keep all of: the source named, every dependent place listed with the term-mention and compiled-in-file examples, a demonstration comparing content to each place, 'not only structure'/'not only its structure'). Also check `cargo test --locked -p athena-context frames` passes, so the file is at most 2097 bytes.
demonstrations.observes: A new bullet in planner.md that states: content that mirrors a governing source needs the source named and every place it depends on listed (each mention of a term, each compiled-in file for a cache key); at least one demonstration compares the written content to those places, not only its structure. The filter `mirror` matches `mirrored_source...` tests (admission.rs, records.rs, outputs.rs), `mirror_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` (refusal_corpus.rs) and `athena_sends_a_plan_that_mirrors_a_source_without_places_back_to_the_planner` (job_plan.rs). Refusal-rule input forms and the corpus case that covers each (all added by step 8, each with its source citing f62n or one of the four introspections): entry with a source and an empty places list -> `mirrored-source-no-places` (Refuse, 'lists no places'); places that are all blank -> `mirrored-source-blank-place` (Refuse, 'lists no places'); blank source -> `mirrored-source-blank-source` (Refuse, 'blank source'); comparison 0 -> `mirrored-source-comparison-zero` (Refuse, 'comparison'); comparison above the criteria count -> `mirrored-source-comparison-out-of-range` (Refuse, 'comparison'); every mention of a term listed -> `mirrored-source-complete-term-mentions` (Accept); every compiled-in cache-key file listed -> `mirrored-source-complete-cache-key-files` (Accept); no entries declared -> `mirrored-source-none-declared` (Accept). The existing corpus cases in `plan_cases` (refusal_corpus.rs:971-993) are unchanged and I read them. demonstrations.observes: Each incomplete plan (no places, only blank places, blank source, comparison 0, comparison above the criteria count) yields exactly one major Athena finding at location `mirrored sources, entry 1` whose summary says the entry lists no places or names the comparison fault. The scripted job (round 1 incomplete, round 2 with the places listed) makes 2 planner calls and 1 critic call, lands (`OutcomeState::Landed`), and the round-2 planner brief contains `lists no places`. The complete plans and the plan with no mirrored sources yield no finding. A comparison that points at a criterion with no demonstration yields only the existing 'needs exactly one' finding.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `mirrored_sources_findings`, the incomplete fixtures yield no finding, so these fail: the admission.rs unit test `a_mirrored_source_with_no_places_is_a_major_finding_naming_the_missing_list`; the corpus case `mirrored-source-no-places` (through `mirror_cases_get_the_expected_outcome`); and the job_plan.rs test `athena_sends_a_plan_that_mirrors_a_source_without_places_back_to_the_planner`. In the last one the round-1 plan would reach the critic, so the total critic calls would be 2, not the asserted 1 (none in round 1), and the round-2 planner brief would not contain `lists no places`. The complete-fixture and no-mirrored-sources cases pass either way, which shows the rule does not refuse good plans.

open_questions: User: Is crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs meant to change? The plan leaves it alone: it holds the queue planner for `athena plan`, not the job plan, and the code for the job-plan section is in admission.rs, run/planning.rs and records.rs.

User: Should a plan that mirrors a source but gives `[]` be caught by a mechanism later, for example a keyword trigger on the reading's criteria? This plan leaves that case to the critic prompt, which is prose-only, because a keyword trigger would also refuse unrelated plans.

User: Should a later change add a mechanical check that each place names a file that exists in the base? This plan declines it because `plan_findings` has no file-exists callback and a place may live in a brief or request rather than the repository.
